main_text.p: & fortitudine audacia imitatur, & patientia durítia immanís, & iusti-tiam acerbitas, & religionem super stitio, & lenitatem mollítia animí, & uerecundiam timiditas, & illam disputandi prudentiã concertatio, captatioȩ uerborum, & hanc ora-toríam uim ínanís quædam pro-fluentía loquendi.

Nam & prudentiã malitia.) Præclarè hic Ci-cero, quæ quamque uirtutem uidentur imitari, uitia enumerat: in quibus enumerandis ordinem suprapositum, & descriptionem uirtutum se-quitur. Quod autem hic opponit prudentiæ ma-liciam, nimiam intelligit calliditatem: quoniam calliditatem ipsam supra in bonis numerauit. Hoc autem præclarum est, quòd fere nobis singu-la uitia ita breuiter describit, & tanquã definit. uelut cũ dicit, esse in uoluptatibus aspernãdis ni-mium studium: & superbiam, in animis extol-lendis affectionem: & despicientiam, in contem-nendis honoribus, abiectionem quandam animi: & effusionem, opum pecuniarumq; immodera-tum sumptum: & audaciã, fortitudinis exuperan-tiam: & duriciam, inanem & efferatam pa-tientiam; & acerbitatem, ius quoddã summum, &

page.notes: Left margin carries cut-off fragments of neighbouring-page marginal words and a few sidenote fragments (illegible, ~a dozen short fragments); not transcribed. The final "&" under the text is a catchword-like mark at the foot of the column and has been placed as a foot note. Several words in the text are doubtful, notably "stitio" (likely superstitio) and "ius quoddã" (likely iustitiæ quoddam), and the mark ")" after "malitia." Long s has been rendered as s throughout.
